claims.text: A DFT-informed machine-learning potential coupled to anharmonic phonon Boltzmann transport and a separate Kubo–Greenwood electronic treatment can predict the lattice and electronic thermal conductivities of HfNbTaTiZr more accurately than previous analytical approaches.
The proposed framework will reduce overall prediction error by at least 30% relative to previous analytical approaches.
The target alloy is equimolar HfNbTaTiZr.
A near-defect-free HfNbTaTiZr bulk structure containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen reflects the relevant experimental condition.
DFT can generate sufficiently accurate energy landscapes and force constants for training the proposed machine-learning potentials.
The machine-learning potentials will be used to sample realistic chemically disordered configurations and anharmonic phonon interactions.
Electronic transport will be computed separately using a Kubo–Greenwood formalism.
The proposed model is applicable from approximately 100 K to 1200 K for HfNbTaTiZr specimens containing around 1 wt.% oxygen.
The lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions of HfNbTaTiZr are comparable below 200 K.
Multielement mixing and oxygen impurities induce configurational disorder and local lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Configurational disorder, local lattice distortion, and oxygen scattering drive anharmonic effects and modify phonon lifetimes and electronic scattering rates.
Explicit disorder sampling and DFT-derived anharmonic force constants allow accurate calculation of phonon mean free paths.
A separate Kubo–Greenwood treatment correctly captures electron scattering independently of lattice vibrations.
Separating phonon and electronic calculations overcomes limitations associated with average Debye temperatures and perfect-crystal approximations.
The proposed method will reproduce total thermal conductivity values of approximately 10–17 W/(m K) at high temperatures.
The proposed method will reproduce distinct, nearly equal lattice and electronic conductivity contributions below 200 K.
Previous predictive simulations conflate lattice and electronic contributions, use Debye-temperature approximations, and assume perfect defect-free crystals.
Model performance outside approximately 100–1200 K, around impurity concentrations substantially different from 1 wt.% oxygen, or under untrained pressures is uncertain.
Low-temperature quantum effects may limit the machine-learning potential's treatment of anharmonic and defect-induced scattering.
Experimental lattice and electronic thermal conductivities can be separately obtained using combined transient thermoreflectance and phonon spectroscopy.

contradictions.description: The central performance claim is a relative reduction of error by at least 30% versus earlier methods, but the falsification rule instead tests whether predictions fall within an absolute 30% error margin. A result could satisfy the latter without demonstrating the claimed relative improvement.
